title: the dotted-address proof compares the launcher's resolved path to its expected path as POSIX on both sides, so it and the launcher proof pass on Windows
intention: The dotted-address proof spells its expected path with as_posix() and compares the launcher's output after turning backslashes into slashes, so the comparison holds on Windows and is unchanged on POSIX.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: the edited proof printed GREEN on Windows (26 mirrored devices, every clause ok) where the unedited one is RED in 4 teeth; the launcher proof that runs it reds only on this proof
traces_to: Law 3: the green was measured by running the edited proof; Law 8: reverting the edit reds both ast teeth on Linux; Law 4: held by a scan, not remembered.
how: In bin/proofs/test_cairn_instance_address.py add a _posix(s) helper, change the five `want = str(root / ...)` lines to `(root / ...).as_posix()` and the five `r.stdout == want + ...` asserts to `_posix(r.stdout) == want + ...`. Red-first proof bin/proofs/test_the_instance_address_proof_compares_posix.py holds both with ast teeth that red on Linux.

clauses.claim: the five expected paths in _clause_a, _clause_b and _fold_before_split are spelled with as_posix(), so test_cairn_instance_address.py passes on Windows
the five stdout compares in those functions go through _posix(), so test_the_launcher_reads_the_bin_beside_the_code, which runs it, passes on Windows

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: the edited proof printed GREEN on Windows (26 mirrored devices, every clause ok) where the unedited one is RED in 4 teeth; the launcher proof that runs it reds only on this proof
measured.how: bin/proofs/test_cairn_instance_address.py run before and after the as_posix edit; bin/proofs/test_the_launcher_reads_the_bin_beside_the_code.py rerun
